citation: Bruti et al. (2024), Biomedicines
title: Insecure Attachment, Oxytocinergic System and C-Tactile Fibers: An Integrative and Translational Pathophysiological Model of Fibromyalgia and Central Sensitivity Syndromes
authors: Gianluca Bruti; Paola Foggetti; Alessandro Rimessi
pain_condition_detail: Fibromyalgia syndrome and central sensitivity syndromes, with discussion of chronic widespread pain, migraine, IBS, low-back pain, post-herpetic neuralgia, CRPS, PTSD, and newborn pain.
context_note: No single country or healthcare system is specified; developmental and social context centers on parent-child dyads, caregiver participation, social support, and social context.
bps_function_set: conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: It operationalizes BPS by turning the chronic-pain model into an attachment–CT–oxytocin neurodevelopmental mechanism: early caregiving/social adversity programs OS/CT systems and stress circuitry, producing emotional dysregulation, inflammation, central sensitization and pain; clinical care is framed as patient-centered and multidisciplinary.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes early social/caregiving adversity and insecure attachment to program OT/CT systems and stress-response circuitry, producing HPA/ANS dysregulation, inflammation, central sensitization, emotional dysregulation, threat perception, and chronic pain; OT/CT stimulation and caregiver/psychological interventions are framed as modifiable targets.
bps_model_variants_1: biopsychosocial model of chronic pain syndromes
emergent_labels_12: Fibromyalgia: Imbalance of Threat and Soothing Systems
conceptual_tensions_1: Small-fiber pathology in FMS is described as unclear in whether it is cause or consequence
conceptual_tensions_2: The discussion contrasts bottom-up nociceptive amplification with descending inhibitory dysfunction
conceptual_tensions_3: The threat/soothing model is questioned as possibly just another representation of ANS dysregulation
conceptual_tensions_4: Intranasal oxytocin for fibromyalgia pain is described as having negative results and limitations
conceptual_tensions_5: The paper states that whether attachment is key in CSSs and functional somatic disorders remains debated
additional_observations_1: The article is a narrative/translational pathophysiological model rather than an evidence synthesis
additional_observations_2: Social content is centered on attachment, caregiving, social support, dyads, and physician-patient relationships rather than work, income, culture, or policy
additional_observations_3: Clinical translation includes intranasal oxytocin, CT-fiber stimulation, psychoeducation, caregiver participation, and physician-patient relationship work
additional_observations_4: Developmental scope spans pregnancy, newborns, infancy, childhood, adolescence, and adulthood
additional_observations_5: The paper uses biomarkers such as HRV, cortisol, IENFD, oxytocin, and inflammatory markers as mechanistic evidence
additional_observations_6: No formal risk-of-bias or quality assessment is reported
synthesis_note: This narrative/translational paper operationalizes BPS as a neurodevelopmental attachment–CT–oxytocin model of fibromyalgia/CSSs. Biological stress, immune, neural and endocrine mechanisms are elaborated; psychological attachment/affect and social caregiving/social support are integrated, but social content is narrow.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined. Biological and psychological content are elaborated; social is mentioned through attachment/caregiving. The triad is mechanistic but narrow.

title: eHealth-Integrated Psychosocial and Physical Interventions for Chronic Pain in Older Adults: Scoping Review
authors: Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso; Leo Benning; Deepak Singh; Annalisa De Lucia; Cinzia Perlini; Alessandro Chiarotto; Sara Pachera; Ilenia Pasini; Lidia Del Piccolo; Valeria Donisi
pain_condition_detail: Chronic noncancer pain in older adults, including osteoarthritis/knee osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and sciatica.
context_note: Included studies were from the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and Thailand; many recruited participants from community-based settings.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review operationalizes BPS mainly by requiring eHealth interventions to combine physical and psychosocial components and by grouping outcomes into pain, psychological, physical, integrated biopsychosocial, and other categories. It synthesizes content and outcomes narratively but does not model cross-domain mechanisms.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper describes BPS as an interaction and lists physical, psychological, and social content or outcomes, but it does not specify mediators, moderators, or cross-domain processes.
quality_assessment_tools_1: quality assessment tool for studies with diverse designs (qatsdd)
bps_model_variants_2: biopsychosocial multimodal approach to CNCP management
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper invokes a BPS interaction but operationalizes it mainly as co-presence of physical and psychosocial components
conceptual_tensions_2: Social content appears as support or context rather than as a mechanism, despite social functioning and social participation being listed
conceptual_tensions_3: The review casts older adults as heterogeneous, but the evidence is concentrated in 65- to 75-year-olds
conceptual_tensions_4: Digital health is framed as improving access, while social support, family/caregiver help, and face-to-face care remain important
conceptual_tensions_5: Pain outcomes rely on self-report and numeric ratings, while the paper notes subjective interpretation and peak-end bias
additional_observations_1: The review excludes stand-alone physical and stand-alone psychosocial eHealth interventions, so the BPS frame is enforced at inclusion rather than analyzed as a mechanism
additional_observations_2: Outcomes are grouped as pain, psychological, physical, integrated biopsychosocial, and other, but pairwise links are mostly listed rather than modeled
additional_observations_3: eHealth delivery is heterogeneous: web-based programs, mHealth, teleconsulting/video consulting, VR, email, websites, smartphone apps, and wearable activity monitors
additional_observations_4: No spiritual or existential constructs are named
additional_observations_5: The article uses QATSDD but not AMSTAR, ROBIS, GRADE, or Cochrane risk of bias
additional_observations_6: Self-determination needs are named without naming self-determination theory
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mostly as an inclusion criterion for eHealth interventions combining physical and psychosocial components and as an outcome taxonomy. It names biological, psychological, and social content, but social factors are contextual and cross-domain links are mostly listed rather than modeled.
coding_rationale: BPS label frames scope and intervention content; biological, psychological, and social domains are present but parallel, with no specified mechanism, so multifactorial.

authors: Hannah Hagy; Esmeralda Hidalgo-Lopez; Christel Portengen; Alexis Holman; Andrew Schrepf; Daniel J. Clauw; Steven E. Harte; Adriene M. Beltz; Amy M. Bohnert; Chelsea M. Kaplan
pain_condition_detail: Primary pain/chronic overlapping pain conditions in adolescents and youth, with emphasis on sex and gender differences emerging during puberty.
context_note: NIH sex-as-biological-variable policy; no specific healthcare system reported.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_usage_sections: abstract; conclusion; other; table or figure
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS as a developmental organizing frame: puberty/CNS mechanisms are linked with behavioral, cognitive-affective, and sociocultural factors to explain female-biased primary pain, but it does not define a formal model or specify a complete causal pathway.
integration_mechanism_summary: Proposed pathways are mostly hypothesized: puberty hormones alter CNS structure/function and pain modulation; sleep and activity interact with CNS connectivity; attention/emotion regulation and sociocultural exposures shape pain reporting, symptoms, and help-seeking. No complete causal model is specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: Sex and gender are described as distinct but difficult to disentangle in primary pain development
conceptual_tensions_2: The model integrates biology, behavior, cognition-affect, and sociocultural factors, but mechanisms remain largely unknown
conceptual_tensions_3: Puberty can be measured as status, timing, or tempo, yet these aspects are often confounded or poorly specified
conceptual_tensions_4: Sex differences can be quantitative, qualitative, latent, or population-based, but many studies control sex rather than model these types
conceptual_tensions_5: Pain is framed as primary/nociplastic without peripheral pathology, yet nociplastic processes can amplify nociceptive pain
additional_observations_1: The paper is explicitly conceptual, not a pooled evidence synthesis, it synthesizes pediatric pain, neuroimaging, and adolescent-development literatures
additional_observations_2: The BPS frame is operationalized through domain headings and future measurement guidance for puberty rather than through named validated pain instruments
additional_observations_3: Female puberty, hormones, and CNS development are foregrounded, research on gender-expansive individuals and sex as a continuum is explicitly noted as lacking
additional_observations_4: The model foregrounds equifinality: no single factor is enough to explain sex differences in primary pain for all youth
additional_observations_5: Precision-treatment recommendations are made without specifying a concrete multimodal intervention
additional_observations_6: Many cross-domain claims are framed as hypotheses or gaps, not as tested effects
synthesis_note: This paper operationalizes BPS as a developmental explanatory model for adolescent primary pain: puberty/hormones and CNS are linked with sleep/activity, attention/emotion regulation, and sociocultural exposures to explain female-biased pain. It is integrative but largely hypothetical, with several named gaps and no tested causal model.
coding_rationale: BPS label is explanatory/organizing; all three domains are substantive and linked through puberty/CNS hypotheses, though no formal definition or tested pathway is specified.

title: Comorbidities Across Functional Neurological Disorder Subtypes: A Comprehensive Narrative Synthesis
authors: Ioannis Mavroudis; Katerina Franekova; Foivos Petridis; Alin Ciobîca; Dăscălescu Gabriel; Emil Anton; Ciprian Ilea; Sotirios Papagiannopoulos; Dimitrios Kazis; Katalin Prokai-Tatrai
pain_condition_detail: Functional neurological disorder (FND) and subtypes: Functional Cognitive Disorder (FCD), Functional Movement Disorder (FMD), Psychogenic Non-Epileptic Seizures (PNES), Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness (PPPD), general/mixed FND, with chronic pain and fibromyalgia comorbidities.
context_note: United Kingdom population estimate; higher rates in industrialized nations; limited cross-ethnic research; diverse groups named including African American, Pacific Islander, Asian, Caucasian, European.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS as a broad explanatory frame for FND comorbidities; organizes evidence by psychiatric versus somatic comorbidity and FND subtype; links biological mechanisms, psychological trauma/stress/cognition, and social context/access. Mostly descriptive clustering and integrated-care rationale, not a specified three-domain mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: No explicit triadic mechanism. Proposed pathways are mostly subtype-level: neural circuit/network dysfunction, interoception/central sensitization, trauma/stress/dissociation, attentional bias, maladaptive beliefs, and social/contextual barriers. PPPD has a behavioral loop, but the social domain remains background.
conceptual_tensions_1: FND is described as lacking structural abnormality, yet the review emphasizes network dysfunction and biomarkers
conceptual_tensions_2: The BPS prism is invoked, but social context is mostly epidemiology, culture, and access rather than an analytic mediator
conceptual_tensions_3: Psychiatric comorbidities dominate several sections, while somatic and pain comorbidities are presented as overlapping but less developed
conceptual_tensions_4: FCD is framed as functional despite overlap with dementia and mild cognitive impairment
conceptual_tensions_5: PRISMA-style selection is used, but the paper states it is not a strict systematic review
additional_observations_1: The paper uses both biopsychological and biopsychosocial vocabulary
additional_observations_2: Comorbidity classification is psychiatric versus somatic/medical, not BPS domains
additional_observations_3: The strongest triadic language appears in the introduction and conclusion, but causal pathways are mostly within bio-psych subdomains
additional_observations_4: PPPD is the clearest example of a behavioral loop involving vestibular instability, hypervigilance, attentional focus, and cognitive schemas
additional_observations_5: Future research calls for longitudinal causal studies, biomarkers, and culturally diverse cohorts
additional_observations_6: No formal BPS definition or operational coding scheme is provided
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as a broad frame for FND comorbidity rather than a coded model. It substantively covers psychiatric constructs and neurobiological mechanisms, while social content is mostly context, culture, access, and gaps. Cross-domain links are mostly descriptive subtype clustering or care recommendations, with limited explicit three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Psych-dominant: psychiatric comorbidities and mechanisms receive most detail; neurobiology is developed, social content thinner. BPS is descriptive/integrative in language, not fully mechanistic triad.

title: The influence of antenatal and pregnancy-related factors on recovery after childbirth: a systematic review
authors: Zayël Z. Frijmersum; Eva Van der Meij; Ralph De Vries; Johannes R. Anema; Judith A.F. Huirne; Petra C.A.M. Bakker
pain_condition_detail: Persistent postpartum genitopelvic or postsurgical pain, urinary incontinence, functional ability, and postpartum mental health outcomes.
context_note: The review frames maternal morbidity as a public health issue and includes English- or Dutch-language studies, but does not report a single country or healthcare system.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: It operationalizes BPS mainly through ICF: recovery outcomes are grouped into physical, mental, functional, and social participation domains, and factors into seven antenatal/pregnancy categories. The paper reports associations and recommends tailored care, but it does not define BPS variables, test a model, or specify cross-domain mechanisms.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper reports associations and recommends combining exercise, mental health support, and workplace adaptations, but does not specify a biological, psychological, or social pathway linking them.
bps_model_variants_3: biopsychosocial approach to antenatal and postpartum care
conceptual_tensions_1: The review’s BPS/ICF framing includes social participation, but no included studies assessed it
conceptual_tensions_2: Physical recovery is the most frequently assessed domain, while functional ability and social participation are underrepresented
conceptual_tensions_3: Physical activity is protective in some included studies but null or adverse in others
conceptual_tensions_4: Age thresholds and outcome definitions vary, limiting comparability across studies
conceptual_tensions_5: Biomedical outcomes dominate despite the stated aim to assess recovery as multidimensional
additional_observations_1: The ICF framework organizes outcomes into physical, mental, functional, and social participation domains, BPS is not converted into measured variables
additional_observations_2: Narrative synthesis was used because study heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis
additional_observations_3: The paper treats lifestyle as a separate category rather than as a pathway linking biological, psychological, and social domains
additional_observations_4: Quality assessment used NOS and RoB 2, no AMSTAR, ROBIS, or GRADE tool is named
additional_observations_5: Social support is framed as potentially modifiable, but only one eligible study evaluated it
additional_observations_6: The paper recommends combining prenatal exercise, mental health support, and workplace adaptations without specifying how these components interact
synthesis_note: The review uses ICF to operationalize a multidimensional recovery frame and groups factors into biomedical, psychological, social, and lifestyle categories. It reports many associations, especially psychological predictors of pain/functional outcomes, but does not define a BPS mechanism or test variables; social participation is absent from included evidence.
coding_rationale: Domains are mostly parallel, with strongest psych-bio and psych-social associations. Social participation is underrepresented. No triadic mechanism is specified.

title: Acoustic stimulation in pain management: neurobiological mechanisms and clinical applications—a narrative review
authors: Jianbo Song; Heng Zhang; Linzhi Wu; Zhengjin Duan; Ge Luo; Meihui Li; Lin He
pain_condition_detail: Acute and chronic pain across perioperative, procedural, cancer, fibromyalgia, low back/neck pain, migraines, phantom limb pain, postherpetic neuralgia, and diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
context_note: Eligibility included all ages, geographical locations, and ethnicities; no specific healthcare system was specified.
bps_function_set: background framing; justification; rhetorical label
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS term is used only to acknowledge pain has biopsychosocial dimensions; the review then operationalizes pain relief through acoustic stimulation mechanisms—CNS, ANS, immune/endocrine, and neurochemical pathways—and clinical AS modalities, with social factors mostly contextual.
integration_mechanism_summary: No true triadic BPS mechanism is proposed. The strongest cross-domain pathway is bio-psychological: AS modulates CNS, autonomic, inflammatory, and endocrine mechanisms that are linked to cognitive processing, anxiety, affect, and pain outcomes. Social factors are mostly contextual moderators or implementation barriers.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper invokes biopsychosocial dimensions but operationalizes the review mainly through neurobiological mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_2: AS is defined as auditory/somatosensory acoustic stimulation, yet immersive VR/AR/MR technologies are included because they integrate acoustic information
conceptual_tensions_3: Acoustic components in immersive technologies are often embedded but not methodologically specified
conceptual_tensions_4: Evidence is concentrated in perioperative pain, fibromyalgia, chronic back pain, and phantom limb pain, while neuropathic pain is sparse
conceptual_tensions_5: Multisensory audiovisual interventions raise placebo and blinding concerns
additional_observations_1: No effect sizes are pooled and no meta-analysis is conducted, the synthesis is narrative despite naming future quality tools
additional_observations_2: The review includes basic research mechanisms and clinical trials/observational studies across all ages and geographies
additional_observations_3: Social factors appear mainly as moderators or implementation barriers rather than explanatory mechanisms
additional_observations_4: Psychological constructs are mostly outcomes or mediators, not a developed analytic domain
additional_observations_5: The conclusion calls for neuroimaging, biochemical markers, and QST to make mechanisms objective
synthesis_note: This review is a neurobiological narrative review that briefly invokes BPS language but does not operationalize BPS as a three-domain model. It codes acoustic stimulation through CNS, autonomic, immune/endocrine, and neurochemical mechanisms, with psychological constructs mostly as pain/affect outcomes or mediators. Social factors are sparse implementation/contextual moderators, so it exemplifies narrow-despite-label use.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined and not used to organize analysis; biological content dominates, psych is present as mechanisms/outcomes, social is thin. Bio-psych integration is mechanistic; triadic integration is only partial.

authors: Xiaofeng Dai; Chongxiang Wang; Ping Jiang; Xiaopeng Mei
pain_condition_detail: Nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic pain.
context_note: UK Biobank data and a 15-center primary care survey are cited; no broader cultural or healthcare-system context is analyzed.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS as an organizing and explanatory frame for pain mechanisms, risk factors, and multimodal care. It operationalizes BPS mainly through nociceptive/neuropathic/nociplastic taxonomy and biological treatment pathways; psychological and social content is present but less developed.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes biological vulnerabilities/injury, stressors/lifestyle, and psychological factors converging on maladaptive neuroplasticity/homeostasis, with a childhood-adversity→catastrophizing pathway. It does not specify a detailed social-to-biological mediator.
conceptual_tensions_1: The abstract presents a systematic synthesis, while the limitations state that the paper is a narrative review, not a systematic review or meta-analysis
conceptual_tensions_2: The BPS frame promises biological, psychological, and social integration, but the paper is dominated by biological mechanism and treatment taxonomy
conceptual_tensions_3: CAP is presented as transformative, yet the paper notes it has not been exhaustively studied for pain relief as a primary endpoint
conceptual_tensions_4: The hippocampus model combines conventional neurobiology with higher-dimensional and Akashic Records language, creating a tension between mechanistic and metaphysical framing
conceptual_tensions_5: Precision pain medicine depends on biomarkers, but the review states that no single definitive biomarker currently diagnoses pain mechanisms
additional_observations_1: The paper uses nociplastic pain as a mechanistic category rather than mapping it directly onto ICD-11 chronic primary pain
additional_observations_2: Psychological constructs are mostly used as therapy targets or risk factors rather than being operationalized through named instruments
additional_observations_3: Social content is thin and mostly limited to support, stressors, adversity, and broad social determinants
additional_observations_4: The BPS operationalization is strongest in the nociplastic pain treatment section
additional_observations_5: CAP and the hippocampus sensor model are original frontiers that may expand the apparent BPS breadth without adding conventional social content
additional_observations_6: No formal quality or risk-of-bias assessment is reported
synthesis_note: The paper invokes BPS as a broad explanatory frame for chronic pain mechanisms and multimodal care, but operationalizes it mainly through mechanism-based nociceptive/neuropathic/nociplastic taxonomy and biological risk/treatment pathways. Psychological factors are named and used in therapy rationale; social content is thin, mainly support/stressors/social determinants. Triadic integration is mostly co-action/synergy rather than a detailed mechanism.
coding_rationale: BPS language is explicit but mostly organizing/explanatory. Biology is elaborated; psych and social are thinner; lifestyle is developed. Triadic integration is descriptive because synergy is asserted, not fully specified.

citation: Cáceres-Matos et al. (2026), Healthcare
title: Biopsychosocial and Cultural Determinants of Functioning and Healthcare Outcomes in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: An Integrative Review
authors: Rocío Cáceres-Matos; Miguel Garrido-Bueno; Juan Manuel Fernández-Sarmiento; Ana María Porcel-Gálvez; Manuel Pabón-Carrasco; Daniele Giansanti
pain_condition_detail: Chronic non-cancer pain (CNCP), including musculoskeletal CNCP, shoulder pain, temporomandibular disorder (TMD), lumbar CNCP, osteoarthritis-related pain, and generalized CNCP.
context_note: European and Spanish prevalence estimates; high-income country predominance with implications for low- and middle-income settings; English/Spanish-only evidence.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS mainly as an organizing and explanatory frame for an integrative review: it extracts biological, psychological, social, and cultural attributes and synthesizes themes, then argues reciprocal interaction. It does not specify a formal BPS measurement model or causal SEM; social content is acknowledged as underexplored.
integration_mechanism_summary: Proposes reciprocal shaping of biological vulnerability, psychological regulation, functional capacity, and social context. Fear-avoidance pathway: pain-related fear -> activity avoidance -> deconditioning -> disability. Social support mitigates emotional distress and pain interference; relational strain/social isolation amplify burden. No formal mediator or quantitative causal model.
quality_assessment_tools_2: scottish intercollegiate guidelines network (sign) levels of evidence framework
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper argues reciprocal BPS interaction, but the evidence base is mostly cross-sectional or observational, limiting causal inference
conceptual_tensions_2: All three domains are integrated in synthesis, yet the authors report social determinants and healthcare quality as underexplored
conceptual_tensions_3: Chronic pain is framed as an ICD-11 diagnostic entity, but included studies vary in operational definitions of chronic pain
conceptual_tensions_4: Social determinants are central to the BPS account, but included evidence is predominately high-income, limiting transferability
conceptual_tensions_5: Clinical practice is described as fragmented and pharmacological despite evidence supporting integrated care
additional_observations_1: The review treats cultural aspects as socially shared meanings and norms, but does not operationalize spirituality or existential suffering
additional_observations_2: Search terms include nursing diagnostic labels such as impaired sleep pattern, impaired mood regulation, and hypervigilance to pain as sensitizing concepts
additional_observations_3: Grey literature search yielded no relevant results to be included in the review
additional_observations_4: The abstract repeats Background and Results paragraphs
additional_observations_5: SAGER guidelines are used for gender reporting, but no gender analysis tool is named
additional_observations_6: Quantitative findings are descriptively summarized and mapped to themes, qualitative data are interpretively synthesized
synthesis_note: The paper presents a genuinely integrative BPS account: it synthesizes biological, psychological, social, and cultural determinants and argues reciprocal interaction. However, its operationalization is thematic and narrative rather than measured or causal; social content is acknowledged as underexplored and much evidence is cross-sectional.
coding_rationale: All three domains are substantively present and linked reciprocally in the narrative, so typology is true_integrative. Integration is mechanistic for bio-psych and psych-social through fear-avoidance and support pathways; triadic integration is descriptive because no formal mediator is specified.

title: Adopting Principles to Guide Pathways: The Best Model for Geriatric Pain Management
authors: Corey B Simon; Stephanie A. Eucker; Kenneth E. Schmader
pain_condition_detail: Older adults with chronic pain, including back pain, knee osteoarthritis, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and neuropathic pain.
context_note: Older adults in geriatric clinical care; VA rural Veterans and insurance-influenced therapy/surgery pathways are examples.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS as a clinical-management frame: explain pain as multifactorial, guide individualized multimodal care, use expectations/communication/function/movement principles, and justify referrals and pain modulators. It does not define variables or test mechanisms.
integration_mechanism_summary: Pain modulators are proposed to calm pain signaling so patients can move; expectations/social context shape treatment engagement; the Pain-Movement Interface gives a feedback-loop account of movement-evoked pain, activity, participation, and biopsychosocial factors. No explicit mediator/moderator across all three domains is specified.
emergent_labels_12: sensitive and hyperactive pain signaling system
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper rejects the idea that pain is reducible to imaging findings, yet still treats degeneration, arthritis, joints, discs, and neuropathic pain as clinically relevant
conceptual_tensions_2: It rejects linear movement from biomedical to psychological to social, but much of the text still lists domain examples before explaining integration
conceptual_tensions_3: It calls for individualized matching to subgroup responses while also emphasizing that trials and care models are heterogeneous and difficult to compare
conceptual_tensions_4: Pain-modulatory interventions are framed as enabling movement, but efficacy and adverse effects vary across individuals
conceptual_tensions_5: Communication is treated as treatment, but the paper also identifies time pressure, agenda overload, and the need for structured follow-up as barriers
additional_observations_1: The paper is a principles-based expert review rather than a formal guideline or evidence synthesis with quality appraisal
additional_observations_2: BPS is operationalized as clinical principles, not as measured constructs or coded variables
additional_observations_3: The paper explicitly names patient resources/handouts but does not report validated patient-reported outcome measures
additional_observations_4: The only named model with explicit cross-domain feedback language is the Pain-Movement Interface
additional_observations_5: Older adults are treated as a population needing modification of interventions, not as the primary evidence base
additional_observations_6: The article frames communication as a clinical skill and treatment component
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS as a geriatric clinical-management frame rather than an empirical model: it lists domains, prioritizes patient-centered explanation, expectations, communication, function, and movement, and cites pain-modulatory interventions. Social factors are named as context, but the only triadic integration is a broad feedback-loop narrative.
coding_rationale: BPS functions mainly as a clinical organizing/intervention frame. Psychological content dominates; social content is named but thin; triadic integration is descriptive rather than mechanistic.

title: Assessing the clinical utility of composite outcomes in studies examining outcomes of implantable neuromodulation therapies for pain: a systematic review
authors: Olivia Soyoung Chung; Gretchen Mae Gabriel; Abeer Alomari; Anuj Bhatia
pain_condition_detail: Chronic refractory pain of moderate-to-severe intensity treated with implantable neuromodulation therapies; includes neuropathy, vascular aetiologies, complex regional pain syndrome, and other causes.
context_note: Country of origin will be extracted; no broader cultural, geographic, or healthcare-system context is otherwise stated.
bps_function_set: justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: It operationalizes BPS as a measurement architecture: extracted outcomes include pain intensity, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation/failure rates, with pain intensity used as comparator. It does not define the model, specify causal pathways, or analyze social determinants.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper links domains by arguing that unidimensional pain intensity and eligibility thresholds miss physical, mental, social, quality-of-life, medication, and explantation outcomes; composite measures are proposed as a measurement architecture, not a causal pathway.
pain_conditions_1: chronic refractory pain of moderate-to-severe intensity
quality_assessment_tools_4: begg’s rank test / egger’s regression test
bps_model_variants_2: complex biopsychosocial nature of chronic pain
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS is invoked to justify multidimensional assessment, but no definition, causal pathway, or social mechanism is provided
conceptual_tensions_2: Pain intensity is criticized as insufficient yet remains the eligibility threshold and comparator outcome
conceptual_tensions_3: Composite outcomes are proposed as a solution, but the paper states no standardized composite outcome currently exists
conceptual_tensions_4: Patient satisfaction is described as important but is not clearly represented in the planned extraction domains
conceptual_tensions_5: Social function and social well-being are named, but extraction focuses on pain, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation
additional_observations_1: This is a protocol, all study conduct and synthesis are future-tense
additional_observations_2: It will extract demographics and country of origin but not social determinants, family, culture, or healthcare access
additional_observations_3: It will standardize pain intensity to a 0–10 scale for comparison
additional_observations_4: It proposes meta-analysis with RevMan and Forest plots, but no BPS model is modelled statistically
additional_observations_5: The BPS frame is measurement-oriented rather than explanatory
synthesis_note: This protocol uses BPS mainly as a justification for composite outcome measures in implantable neuromodulation studies. It names pain intensity, physical health, mental health, quality of life, medication use, and explantation outcomes, with only brief social references. No BPS definition, causal pathway, or social mechanism is proposed; the model is operationalized as a measurement checklist.
coding_rationale: BPS is explicit but undefined. Biological/intervention content is dominant; psychological and social content are named as outcomes only. No cross-domain mechanisms are proposed, supporting pseudo-BPS.

title: Existential therapy for treating chronic pain: A scoping review
authors: Amara Kohlert; Natasha L. Gallant; Taylor G. Hill; Kelsy Dabek
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain; terminal cancer, multiple sclerosis, and chronic non-cancer pain
context_note: Studies came from Germany, the United States, Australia, and Iran; the review excluded non-English publications.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS only to frame existential therapy as holistic and to say health is body, mind, and environment. It does not code studies by BPS domains or operationalize body/mind/environment; data are extracted as intervention/outcome themes, pain outcomes, and existential/spiritual measures.
integration_mechanism_summary: No three-domain mechanism is proposed. The paper proposes that existential or spiritual therapy may reduce pain by decreasing pain sensitivity or reducing negative evaluation of painful experiences, and that spirituality may moderate outcomes; healthcare system gaps are described as context.
emergent_labels_1: Anderson et al., Lima et al
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS to justify holistic care but never operationalizes body, mind, and environment in extraction or analysis
conceptual_tensions_2: Existential or spiritual mechanisms for pain reduction are proposed through pain sensitivity and negative evaluation, but no detailed pathway is given

title: Pain Neuroscience Education in Children and Adolescents with Chronic Pain: A Systematic Review
authors: Mónica Pico; Carmen Matey-Rodríguez; Ana Domínguez-García; Noemí Yubero; Alejandro Santos-Lozano; Laura Papetti; Emma Rheel
pain_condition_detail: Pediatric chronic primary and secondary pain; included headaches, abdominal pain, cervical pain, and musculoskeletal pain.
context_note: Most included studies were educational/school settings; one university hospital, one neurology clinic, and two online studies; socio-educational context noted.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS mainly as a practice frame: PNE is positioned as a component of multidisciplinary programs with exercise, family involvement, and multidimensional measures. It does not define BPS or operationalize it as coded variables; domains are reviewed as outcomes/interventions rather than a specified causal system.
integration_mechanism_summary: PNE is framed to change pain understanding, fear, coping, and self-efficacy, which may reduce pain-related disability and, when combined with exercise, reactivate inhibitory pain processes. PA is described as reducing anxiety/depression/fear and breaking the fear–avoidance cycle. Family involvement is proposed to reduce overprotective responses. No full triadic causal model is specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS is invoked repeatedly, but the paper does not define it or turn it into coded variables
conceptual_tensions_2: PNE is framed as part of multidisciplinary biopsychosocial care, yet most measured effects are cognitive, emotional, or behavioral
conceptual_tensions_3: Pain intensity is treated as a core outcome, but the paper says PNE may work better on cognitive, emotional, and behavioral aspects
conceptual_tensions_4: Family/caregiver involvement is recommended as important, but only four studies included parents or caregivers
conceptual_tensions_5: Digital, gamified, and VR delivery formats are promising, but their effectiveness and sustained outcomes remain unclear
additional_observations_1: The review excludes procedural, oncological, primary neurological condition, and recurrent acute pain
additional_observations_2: Most included studies were clinical or pilot trials in school/educational settings, one university hospital, one neurology clinic, and two online studies were reported
additional_observations_3: PNE content was based on international PNE guidelines by Butler and Moseley and Louw and Puentedura
additional_observations_4: Online cognitive behavioral therapy was a comparator/control in Web-MAP2 studies
additional_observations_5: Sex/gender is discussed as both biological and sociocultural
additional_observations_6: Family/caregiver involvement is framed as underused but important for sustainable pediatric chronic pain care
synthesis_note: This pediatric PNE review uses BPS mainly as a practice frame for multidisciplinary care. It extracts PNE effects on pain knowledge, self-efficacy, fear/catastrophizing, function, sleep, parental responses, and some biological markers, but rarely specifies how domains interact. Social content is mostly family/school/system context. BPS is invoked to justify comprehensive care, not operationalized as a three-domain model.
coding_rationale: BPS language mainly justifies multidisciplinary care and multidimensional outcomes. Bio/psych are substantive; social is thinner. Pairwise mechanisms appear, but no full triadic causal model.

citation: Strien & Hollmann (2025), The European Journal of Neuroscience
title: Pain Perception and Modulation: Fundamental Neurobiology and Recent Advances
authors: Willem W. J. van Strien; Markus W. Hollmann
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; justification
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS label is used to justify breadth and variability in pain, but the review operationalizes pain mainly as neurobiology: circuits, synapses, receptors, neuromodulators, and neuromodulation. Psychological and sociocultural factors are named as influences on pain perception; no psychosocial constructs are measured and no social mechanism is specified.
integration_mechanism_summary: Several bio-psych pathways are proposed: stress and mood can bidirectionally worsen chronic pain; PFC-PAG and PFC neurons modulate pain via descending inhibition; PVT-BLA and LC pathways link pain with anxiety/depression. No social mechanism is specified; social factors are only listed.
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS acknowledges psychological and sociocultural shaping of pain, yet the review's substantive content is almost entirely neurobiological
conceptual_tensions_2: Pain is framed as subjective and multidimensional, but operationalized through circuits, receptors, and neuromodulators
conceptual_tensions_3: Human clinical variability is the target, but much mechanistic evidence comes from rodents
conceptual_tensions_4: Women are noted as more prevalent in chronic pain, while preclinical studies primarily use male rodents
conceptual_tensions_5: Neuromodulation is presented as potentially reshaping circuits, but clinical effects are modest or variable
additional_observations_1: No psychological, social, or BPS construct is operationalized with validated questionnaires in the review
additional_observations_2: The only social domain content is "sociocultural factors" and insula-related "social behavior"
additional_observations_3: Personalized pain management is grounded in systems-level neurobiology rather than measured BPS variables
additional_observations_4: The review treats placebo/nocebo expectations as psychological influences on pain perception but does not analyze them as a framework
additional_observations_5: The article distinguishes nociception from pain, which counters a common construct conflation
additional_observations_6: The review cites ICD-11 to frame chronic pain as a disease in its own right
synthesis_note: This narrative review uses the BPS label mainly to frame chronic pain as subjective and variable, but its operational content is a systems-level neurobiology review. It names psychological and sociocultural influences and many bio-psych pathways, yet social factors are not developed or measured and no three-domain mechanism is specified.
coding_rationale: Bio is elaborated; psych is elaborated; social is only mentioned. Bio-psych integration is mechanistic, psych-social none, triadic partial. BPS typology is pseudo_bps.

title: Sex-Related Differences in Chronic Pain: A Narrative Review by a Multidisciplinary Task Force
authors: Maurizio Marchesini; Diego Fornasari; Silvia Natoli; Elena Vegni; Arturo Cuomo; Allison B. Reiss
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain (CP), defined as pain persisting for over 3 months, with sex-related differences in prevalence, perception, and treatment response.
context_note: Italian expert task force; prevalence examples from Italy and Western countries.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS by listing sex and gender differences, symptoms, physiological indicators, medical history, lifestyle, and psychological aspects as factors to consider, then organizing evidence into biological, psycho-social, treatment, and adverse-drug sections. It rarely specifies cross-domain pathways.
integration_mechanism_summary: No explicit cross-domain mechanism is specified. The review repeatedly states that biological, psycho-social, and socio-economic factors interact and influence pain experiences, treatment response, and outcomes, but it does not name a mediator or pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: Sex and gender are explicitly conflated while the review calls for a more nuanced understanding of both
conceptual_tensions_2: BPS is invoked as operational, but the paper lists factors without formally defining the model or specifying cross-domain mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_3: Women constitute the majority of CP sufferers, yet research and clinical trials are described as historically male-biased
conceptual_tensions_4: Sex-specific analgesic and opioid findings are mixed and attributed to differences in experimental design, pain stimulus type, and sample size
conceptual_tensions_5: Psychological therapy is recommended, but patients may misunderstand it as implying pain is psychosomatic or “in their head”
additional_observations_1: The review is narrative and expert-driven, with literature critically appraised but no formal risk-of-bias or quality tool named
additional_observations_2: The paper uses both “psycho-social” and “biopsychosocial,” but the hyphenated psycho-social term is more common in the body
additional_observations_3: Treatment sections emphasize pharmacology, adverse drug reactions, pharmacokinetics, and sex-disaggregated trial data more than psychosocial care
additional_observations_4: The paper reports sex-disaggregated prevalence and outcomes but does not pool evidence or provide effect estimates
additional_observations_5: Lifestyle appears only as a BPS component in the abstract and is not elaborated substantively
additional_observations_6: Care settings span clinical practice, pain clinics, pain rehabilitation programs, clinical trials, and population surveys
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly by listing sex/gender, biological, psycho-social, and socio-economic factors and organizing evidence into sex-difference sections. It offers several directional associations (SES, mental health, support, treatment response) but little named mechanism. Overall, it is a descriptive true-integrative narrative with bio-psych emphasis and social content mostly as modifiers of care and outcomes.
coding_rationale: Bio and psych are elaborated; social is substantive but thinner. Triadic integration is descriptive, not mechanistic; BPS is used to organize and justify sex-aware care.

title: Knowledge, mechanisms, and intervention of the polytrauma clinical triad in military pain medicine
authors: Qinghua Liu; Peipei Qiu; Tao Ma; Yali Zhao; Shihui Fu; Minglong Gao; Zeguo Feng; Long Feng
pain_condition_detail: Post-traumatic chronic pain, post-traumatic stress disorder, and traumatic brain injury in active-duty service members and veterans.

bps_function_set: conclusion; intervention rationale; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS label is not operationalized as variables; the paper uses PCT to organize chronic pain, PTSD, and TBI, then discusses mechanisms and treatments. BPS appears mainly to justify interdisciplinary, multimodal care.
integration_mechanism_summary: No fully triadic mechanism. The paper proposes bio-psych mechanisms such as chronic stress neuroendocrine/immune/metabolic mediators affecting cognition/mood, brain injury/disorganized pain modulation, and pain-sleep aggravation; social factors are mostly consequences or care-system contexts.
conceptual_tensions_1: Although each disease of this triad could occur in isolation, it is valuable to know whether a single condition increases the risk of the entire triad and whether the rest of PCT needs to be screened for
conceptual_tensions_2: the survival rate of wounded soldiers has exceeded 90%, but the treatment rate for pain is not as high as the survival rate [ - ]
conceptual_tensions_3: opioids are the most efficacious agents for acute and chronic pain associated with neurological or tissue injury [ ]
conceptual_tensions_4: Opioids are not currently recommended as the first treatment for any type of chronic pain in clinical practice, and even many guidelines do not recommend their use in specific populations such as younger groups with non-cancerous pain [ ]
conceptual_tensions_5: Because neurobiological mechanisms of PTSD are not well established, available pharmacological treatment options are currently limited
additional_observations_1: PCT, not a formal BPS model, is the paper's main organizing unit
additional_observations_2: Social content is mostly about work, family burden, VHA/military health systems, and costs rather than social determinants of pain
additional_observations_3: The BPS label appears only in the abstract and conclusion
additional_observations_4: The paper's strongest integration is between pain, PTSD/TBI, sleep, cognition, and suicide risk

additional_observations_6: Sleep is treated both as a clinical complication and as a lifestyle/treatment target

title: Pain Neuroscience Education on Reducing Opioid Dependency in African American and Caucasian Populations: A Narrative Review
authors: Austin Granger; Ersilia Mirabelli; Masahiro Kohzuki
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain with nociplastic mechanisms and opioid use disorder in African American and Caucasian patients in a physical therapy setting.
context_note: American focus on African American and Caucasian populations; disparities in prescribing, access, provider bias, trust, socioeconomic status, and cultural pain beliefs.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS by using systems/ecological theory to organize a narrative review of nociplastic pain mechanisms, opioid prescribing disparities, pain beliefs, and PNE. PNE is framed as a biopsychosocial intervention that changes faulty pain cognitions, stress/fear/anxiety, and trust-related processing to reduce opioid dependence; no variables are tested as a formal BPS model.
integration_mechanism_summary: Proposed pathways are narrative: PNE changes faulty pain cognitions and stress/fear/anxiety, which may calm central processing and reduce pain and opioid use; pain beliefs, provider trust, and ethnic disparities modulate pain processing and opioid prescribing/access. No tested causal model is reported.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS to critique biomedical reductionism, yet its evidence base is narrative and cannot make causal claims
conceptual_tensions_2: Ethnic disparities are used as explanatory factors, but the paper cautions that individual pain responses remain unique
conceptual_tensions_3: PNE is framed as promising for reducing opioid dependence, but no statistical analysis or experimental design is included
conceptual_tensions_4: Provider trust and provider ethnicity are proposed as modulators of pain brain activity, but the review reports this as future research
conceptual_tensions_5: Social support is treated as important, yet studies disagree and qualitative perspectives are called for
additional_observations_1: The review includes quantitative, qualitative, and other review articles in its methods
additional_observations_2: Search terms cover central sensitization, peripheral processing mechanisms, central processing mechanisms, ion channel expression, pain neuromatrix, and graded motor imagery
additional_observations_3: PNE is consistently framed as adjunctive to physical therapy, especially active movement, GMI, manual therapy, or exercise therapy
additional_observations_4: OUD is treated as a chronic disorder with physical, social, and mental health implications rather than only a substance-use outcome
additional_observations_5: Buprenorphine is discussed as affecting depression, anxiety, stress, and quality of life in OUD recovery
additional_observations_6: The paper calls for fMRI studies comparing PNE and GMI across ethnicities
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS as a systems/ecological rationale for PNE in chronic pain and OUD. It links nociplastic mechanisms, pain beliefs, provider trust, prescribing disparities, and social support, but the integration is narrative and largely cross-domain association rather than tested causal modelling.
coding_rationale: True integrative because all three domains are linked through PNE, pain beliefs, disparities, and neuroplasticity; no formal BPS model is tested.

title: Neurobiology of Chronic Pain, Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, and Mild Traumatic Brain Injury
authors: Gerald Young; Hella Thielen; Kristin Samuelson; Joel Jin; Ioannis Mavroudis; Dimitrios A. Kazis
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain, concussion/mild traumatic brain injury (MTBI), and fear/posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
context_note: Forensic/disability-assessment and court context is emphasized; legal-related and secondary-gain motivations are discussed.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper embeds central/peripheral sensitization in the biological component of BPS and posits psychological reserve/control plus social factors as exacerbations. It uses BPS mainly as a causal scaffold, not as measured variables or a tested three-domain model.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes several top-down/bottom-up pathways: threat appraisal triggers fear and avoidance, which prevents habituation and exacerbates sensory sensitization; GABA–glutamate imbalance increases excitability/arousal/attention, linked to sensory hypersensitivity; pain/fatigue and poor sleep deplete reserve and weaken control. Social/legal factors are described as exacerbating or motivating symptoms, but no full triadic pathway is specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS as a broad causal frame but its substantive mechanism is overwhelmingly neurobiological sensitization
conceptual_tensions_2: It generalizes sensitization from chronic pain to MTBI and PTSD while noting direct evidence is limited or lacking
conceptual_tensions_3: It searches for biomarkers but concludes that none are definitive, even while arguing for neurobiological underpinnings
conceptual_tensions_4: The social domain is mostly forensic/legal/secondary-gain content rather than socioeconomic, family, or healthcare-system content
conceptual_tensions_5: The court context treats chronic pain without tissue damage as controversial despite the article's physiological/neurological framing
additional_observations_1: Chronic pain is treated as one component of a broader psychological-injury-and-law frame, alongside MTBI and PTSD
additional_observations_2: The article is a scoping-style literature review of neurobiology rather than a psychosocial intervention review
additional_observations_3: It names several instruments and diagnostic systems, but they are used conceptually or as cited measures rather than pooled in a meta-analysis
additional_observations_4: The paper's integration is strongest at neural and cognitive-behavioral levels and thinnest at the social level
additional_observations_5: The BPS label does explanatory and therapeutic work, but the paper does not operationalize BPS as measured variables or formal constructs
additional_observations_6: The paper repeatedly distinguishes biological mechanisms from forensic/legal interpretations of psychological injury
synthesis_note: The article uses BPS mainly as a causal scaffold around neurobiological sensitization. Biological content is developed; psychological concepts are linked through reserve/control, fear-avoidance, and attention networks; social content is mostly forensic/legal. It proposes some top-down/bottom-up pathways but not a full three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Bio-dominant pseudo-BPS: all domains appear, but social/legal factors are thin and triadic reasoning remains partial.

title: Pain Reprocessing Therapy – Schmerz neu denken
authors: Antje Kallweit; Howard Schubiner
pain_condition_detail: Chronic primary/noziplastic pain, especially chronic back pain; includes fibromyalgia, CRPS I, primary head/mouth/face pain, primary visceral pain, and primary musculoskeletal pain.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_usage_sections: abstract; conclusion; discussion; introduction; table or figure
bps_operationalization_summary: PRT operationalizes BPS as a structured psychotherapeutic package for nociplastic pain: pain education plus mindfulness, graded exposure, cognitive restructuring, emotional processing, self-efficacy, and neuroplastic relearning. It links fear-avoidance processes to brain alarm-system mechanisms; social content is mainly outpatient implementation, work/family, and stress.
integration_mechanism_summary: Noziplastic pain is framed as a brain-generated warning signal maintained by central sensitization and fear-avoidance processes. PRT aims to calm the alarm system through education, exposure, cognitive restructuring, emotional processing, and self-efficacy. Social factors mainly enter as stress, work/family context, and outpatient implementation rather than a full social-biological pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS language while the social domain remains thin compared with nociplastic neurobiology and fear-avoidance psychology
conceptual_tensions_2: PRT claims to integrate biopsychosocial approaches but is explicitly described as strongly neurocentric
conceptual_tensions_3: The paper treats chronic primary pain as without tissue or nerve damage while also requiring careful exclusion of structural, inflammatory, infectious, tumor-related, and neuropathic causes
conceptual_tensions_4: PRT is presented as promising and guideline-concordant, but the evidence base is described as young, small, and not yet supported by systematic reviews
conceptual_tensions_5: Implementation in ambulant care is recommended, yet time, resources, therapist training, manuals, and standardized education are named as practical barriers
additional_observations_1: The first paragraph pairs pain factors as “psychosozial und somatisch”, making the article’s BPS structure a side-by-side opposition rather than a detailed mechanism
additional_observations_2: The article’s BPS use is strongest as a practical implementation rationale for PRT and weakest as a social determinants framework
additional_observations_3: Several social elements are embedded in the case example rather than developed as general social mechanisms
additional_observations_4: The paper’s main pathway is psychological reinterpretation and emotional processing changing brain-generated pain signals
additional_observations_5: The article treats diagnostic algorithms and structured instruments as ways to identify nociplastic mechanisms rather than as measures of a broad BPS model
additional_observations_6: The conclusion moves from a specific PRT intervention to a broad paradigm shift toward modern pain medicine
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as a rationale for implementing PRT in chronic primary/noziplastic pain. It elaborates nociplastic neurobiology and fear-avoidance/self-efficacy processes, links them through central sensitization, neuroplasticity, and the fear-pain cycle, but social content is mostly outpatient care, work/family, stress, and implementation.
coding_rationale: BPS functions mainly as intervention rationale; bio-psych integration is mechanistic, social is thin, triadic integration partial.

citation: Guerra-Armas et al. (2025), Healthcare
title: Harnessing Extended Reality for Neurocognitive Training in Chronic Pain: State of the Art, Opportunities, and Future Directions
authors: Javier Guerra-Armas; Alberto Roldán-Ruiz; Mar Flores-Cortes; Daniel S. Harvie; Paolo Cotogni
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain conditions, with neurocognitive impairments, across nociplastic, neuropathic, musculoskeletal, secondary headache or orofacial, cancer-related, post-surgical, sports injury-related, post-stroke, and complex regional pain syndrome contexts.
context_note: International population framing (“worldwide”); focus is rehabilitation/clinical implementation rather than a specific country or healthcare system.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS mainly as a framing and intervention rationale for XR-based neurocognitive training. It operationalizes the model through neurocognitive impairments as transdiagnostic vulnerability factors and multimodal rehabilitation, while social content is mostly implementation context rather than a coequal mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: Bio-psych mechanism proposed: chronic pain can drain cognitive resources, alter brain networks and neural plasticity, and disrupt sensorimotor control; attention, emotion, and memory mediate XR effects on descending pain modulation and neuroplasticity. Social content is mainly implementation context; no three-domain pathway is specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: Although the paper says different factors interact, it does not specify how biological, psychological, and social factors jointly produce XR response
conceptual_tensions_2: Neurocognitive functions are central but the paper says they lack consensus definition/use
conceptual_tensions_3: The transdiagnostic approach seeks shared mechanisms, while pain phenotypes may moderate XR effects
conceptual_tensions_4: XR is framed as promising, but evidence is preliminary, heterogeneous, and not compared with non-XR cognitive training
conceptual_tensions_5: Implementation barriers include costs, limited validated games, cybersickness, and lack of protocols
additional_observations_1: The review is transdiagnostic and explicitly excludes experimental or acute pain
additional_observations_2: Final synthesis included n = 23 studies
additional_observations_3: No specific pain, neurocognitive, or psychosocial scale is named, standardized cognitive assessment tools are only recommended
additional_observations_4: XR is defined as an umbrella term for AR, VR, and MR
additional_observations_5: The paper recommends reporting frameworks rather than reporting a formal risk-of-bias assessment
additional_observations_6: The social domain appears mainly through clinical implementation, costs, stakeholders, and policymakers
synthesis_note: This paper operationalizes BPS mainly as a framing and intervention rationale for XR neurocognitive training in chronic pain. It develops neurocognitive/psychological mechanisms and links them to pain, but social content is mostly implementation context. The paper does not provide a full three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Explicit BPS language is present but not a defined model. Bio-psych pathways are mechanistic; social content is thin; triadic integration is partial because social factors are mostly contextual.

citation: Muacevic et al. (2025), Cureus
title: Beyond the Biomedical Model: A Critical Review of the Approach to Chronic Pain and the Proposal of an Integrated Functional Model
authors: Alexander Muacevic; John R Adler; Luigi Pianese; Bruno Bordoni
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain broadly, including chronic low back pain, chronic headache/migraine, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic fatigue syndrome, and chronic pelvic pain.
context_note: Global adult population; Europe and United States prevalence and cost figures are reported.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; critique or problematization; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS mainly as a critique/organizing frame, then substitutes a functional model. It lists biological, psychological, nutritional, environmental, and social factors and proposes multimodal assessment/interventions, but it does not code or measure BPS variables in an empirical dataset.
integration_mechanism_summary: The proposed model posits that biological terrain, especially the extracellular matrix, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, nutrition, environment, lifestyle, psychological/behavioral factors, and social factors converge on peripheral and central nociceptive sensitization. Social exclusion is linked to shared brain circuits; social determinants influence incidence/prognosis. No BPS-specific mediators are measured.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper criticizes the biomedical model for ambiguity between pain as alarm, symptom, and disease while also noting that ICD classification may medicalize pain
conceptual_tensions_2: BPS is credited with integrating biological, psychological, and social factors, but the paper argues it neglects nutrition, lifestyle, environment, and extracellular matrix mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_3: The proposed functional model is presented as more complete, yet the paper also states that research on it is still in its infancy
conceptual_tensions_4: Social factors are conceptually recognized in BPS, but the paper says they have received less empirical attention than psychological factors
conceptual_tensions_5: The paper emphasizes poor correlation between tissue damage and pain perception while also discussing structural lesions as part of biomedical explanations
additional_observations_1: This is a narrative review, not a systematic review, no formal quality or risk-of-bias assessment is reported
additional_observations_2: The paper does not empirically operationalize BPS variables through measures, coding, or pooled data
additional_observations_3: The functional dimension is treated as a fourth dimension added to biological, psychological, and social domains
additional_observations_4: Most mechanistic claims are citation-based or conceptual rather than tested within the review
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as a critique of biomedicine and then replaces it with a bio-psycho-functional-social model. Biological/functional mechanisms dominate; psychological and social factors are named and linked to pain, but the paper provides more mechanistic claims for biological terrain and lifestyle/environment than for social pathways. It does not empirically operationalize BPS variables.
coding_rationale: Biological/functional content dominates and is mechanistically developed; psychosocial content is named and linked to pain. The proposed model integrates all domains through matrix/inflammation pathways, so true_integrative despite BPS being critiqued.

bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS only as an adjacent label for precision-medicine pain management. citation: Aboushaar & Serrano (2024), Frontiers in Pain Research
title: The mutually reinforcing dynamics between pain and stress: mechanisms, impacts and management strategies
authors: Nour Aboushaar; Natalia Serrano
pain_condition_detail: Chronic pain and recurrent/episodic pain, with examples including tension-type headaches, migraine, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, and chronic low back/neck/shoulder pain.
context_note: Worldwide framing; includes American adults and workplace/financial stressors; discusses racial/ethnic and socioeconomic disparities in pain care.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS as a triadic mechanism map: physiological processes, cognitive/behavioral responses, and social/lifestyle/environmental factors explain a pain-stress vicious cycle and justify holistic pharmacological, psychological, lifestyle, and social/environmental management.
integration_mechanism_summary: No single triadic mechanism is specified; the review describes reciprocal pain-stress reinforcement mediated by allostatic/neuroendocrine/inflammatory processes, cognitive/behavioral responses, and social/lifestyle/environmental factors, then uses that account to justify holistic multimodal management.
conceptual_tensions_1: The article contrasts the IASP pain definition emphasizing sensory and experiential aspects with broader accounts recognizing cognitive and social aspects
conceptual_tensions_2: Pain origin categories are presented as useful for diagnosis and treatment but explicitly not mutually exclusive and often overlapping
conceptual_tensions_3: Pain and stress responses are described as adaptive and protective yet maladaptive when recurrent or persistent
conceptual_tensions_4: Social support is protective, but pain can reduce social relationships and support
conceptual_tensions_5: The review uses BPS language to integrate mechanisms but does not provide a formal BPS model definition or instruments
additional_observations_1: The evidence synthesis is narrative/expert rather than systematic, no quality assessment or risk-of-bias method is reported
additional_observations_2: The case study operationalizes the vicious cycle through a hypothetical adult with workplace stress, overweight, inactivity, poor diet, sleep disruption, anxiety, and medication use
additional_observations_3: Stress is coded here as both a physiological/psychological response and a social stressor, expanding beyond a narrow chronic-pain review
additional_observations_4: Lifestyle/environmental factors are substantively developed but are not one of the three core domains scored in domain_evidence
additional_observations_5: The article uses neuroimaging findings to connect psychological interventions to pain-modulation brain networks
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS as a pain-stress vicious-cycle account rather than a formal model. It gives detailed neuroendocrine/inflammatory and cognitive-behavioral mechanisms, plus SES, social support, work, diet, activity, substance use, and sleep. The strongest integration is reciprocal bio-psych and psych-social; triadic integration is descriptive and used to justify holistic multimodal care.
coding_rationale: BPS is used as an organizing/explanatory frame; all core domains are elaborated and relationally linked. Triadic integration is descriptive rather than a single specified mechanism.

title: Integrated Approach to Chronic Pain—The Role of Psychosocial Factors and Multidisciplinary Treatment: A Narrative Review
authors: Irena Kovačević; Jadranka Pavić; Biljana Filipović; Štefanija Ozimec Vulinec; Boris Ilić; Davorina Petek; Cesar Fernández-de-las-Peñas
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
pain_condition_detail: Chronic non-malignant pain, with examples of chronic primary pain, chronic secondary musculoskeletal pain, chronic neuropathic pain, chronic postsurgical/posttraumatic pain, and low back pain.
context_note: Cites European and U.S. adult prevalence and discusses primary healthcare access, healthcare-system sustainability, and multidisciplinary pain centers.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_usage_sections: abstract; conclusion; discussion; introduction; methods; other
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the BPS label mainly to justify multidisciplinary chronic pain treatment: physical training/patient education, CBT/psychological interventions, and work/social-environment discussions are listed as components. It does not test or specify a three-domain mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: No explicit cross-domain mechanism is proposed. The paper asserts interactions and treatment effects, with directional claims such as psychological impact on pain intensity and social support on activation/pain tolerance, but pathways and mediators are not specified.
conceptual_tensions_1: Chronic pain is defined by duration in more than one way: exceeding expected recovery, lasting more than three months, or lasting longer than six months
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper invokes a complex biopsychosocial interplay but mostly lists biological, psychological, and social factors or interventions side by side
conceptual_tensions_3: The umbrella term chronic non-malignant pain covers chronic primary, secondary musculoskeletal, neuropathic, postsurgical/posttraumatic, headache/orofacial, visceral, and cancer-related categories
conceptual_tensions_4: Psychological constructs receive definitions or operational tools more often than social constructs, despite the paper calling for greater social emphasis
conceptual_tensions_5: The review evaluates treatment approaches through a non-systematic narrative method without reporting formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal
additional_observations_1: The paper positions chronic pain as a human right and global public health priority
additional_observations_2: The search strategy includes MeSH terms Chronic Pain, Pain Management, and Models, Biopsychosocial
additional_observations_3: Virtual reality is introduced as promising but preliminary, not synthesized as an established BPS component
additional_observations_4: Multidisciplinary team composition is specified, but the team model is not evaluated as an implementation mechanism
additional_observations_5: Primary healthcare is framed as the access point for early treatment and return to work
additional_observations_6: The review reports 120 papers but does not provide a formal synthesis method or appraisal results
synthesis_note: This narrative review operationalizes BPS mainly as a clinical rationale for multidisciplinary chronic pain management. It names biological, psychological, and social factors and interventions, but the domains are mostly asserted or listed rather than connected through explicit mechanisms.
coding_rationale: BPS label primarily justifies multidisciplinary care; all domains present but mostly parallel/asserted. Triadic integration is descriptive, not mechanistic.
